title: Oral thrush
intro: Oral thrush is a fungal infection of the mouth caused by Candida yeast. It produces creamy white patches on the tongue and cheeks, soreness and a cottony feeling. It is common in babies, older people, people using inhaled steroids or dentures and those with weakened immunity. It is usually easy to treat.

sections.heading: Causes
paragraphs: Candida normally lives in small numbers in the mouth. It can overgrow after antibiotics, with dry mouth, when using inhaled or oral corticosteroids, with diabetes, after chemotherapy, with HIV or in smokers. Dentures that fit poorly and are not cleaned well can harbour yeast.

sections.heading: Symptoms
paragraphs: White or yellowish patches that can be scraped off, leaving red, sore areas, are typical. Other symptoms include a burning mouth, loss of taste, cracks at the corners of the mouth and discomfort when eating or swallowing. Babies may refuse feeds and show white patches inside the cheeks.

sections.heading: Treatment
paragraphs: Antifungal gels, drops or lozenges are used in the mouth for about a week or as directed, and continued for a couple of days after symptoms resolve. Tablets are used for severe or persistent infections. Rinse your mouth after using inhaled steroids. Clean dentures and soak them overnight in antifungal solution as advised. Breastfeeding mothers may need treatment of the nipples too.

sections.heading: Prevention
paragraphs: Brush teeth twice daily, clean dentures, avoid wearing dentures at night, stop smoking, control blood sugar and keep your mouth moist. Sterilise baby bottle teats and dummies.

sections.heading: When to seek help
paragraphs: See a doctor if thrush lasts more than two weeks, recurs often, causes difficulty swallowing or occurs without a clear reason, as it can signal underlying disease.

examples.title: Treating a baby
examples.text: Imagine your baby has white patches inside the cheeks. You could ask the doctor or pharmacist for a suitable antifungal gel, clean dummies and bottle teats carefully and use the medicine for the full period.

examples.title: Caring for dentures
examples.text: Suppose you wear dentures and have a sore tongue. You might leave dentures out at night, clean them thoroughly and ask your dentist or doctor about antifungal treatment.
